<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **1** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bdd51769ee827b24355fa1328375bb09c05c8d65` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a587a72a1f20b8bc8d26ba76e638188a985ddad1` — the merge of head `69b88800e2ce07d7cf664de8af3c3430a6fd2d19` into base `bdd51769ee827b24355fa1328375bb09c05c8d65`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a587a72a1f20b8bc8d26ba76e638188a985ddad1 && git checkout a587a72a1f20b8bc8d26ba76e638188a985ddad1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bdd51769ee827b24355fa1328375bb09c05c8d65 69b88800e2ce07d7cf664de8af3c3430a6fd2d19 && git checkout -B drift-repro bdd51769ee827b24355fa1328375bb09c05c8d65 && git merge --no-ff 69b88800e2ce07d7cf664de8af3c3430a6fd2d19

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bdd51769ee827b24355fa1328375bb09c05c8d65
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs bdd51769ee827b24355fa1328375bb09c05c8d65` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**L1 verdict: REWORK (2 items, both about PR text and card bookkeeping, not code)** · card #34448 · area o2-C · first review · read at 2026-11-16T23:33Z
Head-sha: `69b88800e2ce07d7cf664de8af3c3430a6fd2d19`. This is the final head announced on this PR, and all 53 check runs are on it.

The code, tests and evidence pass L1 as they stand at this head. Neither rework item needs a push. Both are a body edit or a card filing, so the head stays where it is, and the delta read is the body only.

### Rework items

1. **`Fixes #34448` → `Part of #34448`.** Acceptance item 4 of the card asks for one live `asset_lifecycle` re-run showing six of six operations measured per half. This PR's Acceptance notes record it as NOT MEASURED (no model credential in the container), with the seat's daily gallery task as the carrier. A merge with `Fixes` would close the card before its last acceptance item is read. Please change the first card line to `Part of #34448` with no verb next to the number. Put the closing arrangement in a comment on the card, not in the body: the card closes when the live run reads 6/6 per half, and `pm:dispatched` is removed by hand then.
2. **Template-mode follow-up needs a destination.** The report's `out_of_scope_findings` says "template mode's write-back restore still meets an app's one-way rule … noted, not filed", with carrier none. The dev recommends filing it (open question 3, option A). Before landing, the area or seat files that card, or records on #34448 why it is not filed. Then add its number to the PR body's Acceptance notes as a plain reference with no closing verb.

### Checklist readings (pass)

- **Shape.** Draft, base `main`, `mergeable_state: clean`. A closing-keyword scan of the body finds only `Fixes #34448` (item 1).
- **File surface** (`get_files`, 4 files, +345/-66): `packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/orchestrate.ts`, `test/runner/orchestrate.test.ts`, `packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`, and `.changeset/34448-scenario-fresh-copy-restore.md`. These match the claim as amended (comment 6931982958, which added the README bullet and the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line). No `content/docs/releases/` change.
- **Premise correction.** Ask 1 (a privileged restore path) is reported as having no path without weakening the platform. The report names `importControlOptOutRefusal` and `importUndoWriteContext`, and the runner reaches the app over HTTP only. The card itself names Ask 2 as the fallback, and the PR takes it and states the cost. The dev's correction is written in the PR body.
- **Fix, read in the diff.**
  - `runHalf` takes an optional trailing `fresh: FreshCopy`.
  - Before each operation it now only reads (`seedDrift`, which reuses the former read loop of `restoreSeededRows`). On drift, `moveToFreshCopy` seeds a new copy and compares it with the run's seed (`seedDifference`: inserted count, refusals with code and fields, permission-set assignment). Only then does it switch `app`, `adminKey`, `seeded` and `accounts`.
  - `keyOf` and `doorOf` read those `let` bindings when called, so later turns go to the copy.
  - Copies are released in the replaced-copy path, the failure path and the half's `finally`. The booted app stays with `withApp`.
  - Copies do not share state. `bootDev` takes a `freePort()` per boot and runs `objectstack dev --fresh`, which gets its own ephemeral DB (`packages/cli/src/commands/dev-default-db.test.ts`, "yields to --fresh (its own ephemeral temp DB…)").
  - Template mode passes no `fresh`, and a comment at the call explains why.
- **Changeset.** `@objectstack/scenarios` publishes (no `private` in `package.json`), so a patch changeset is owed, and one is present. Its body carries `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` at line start. I checked its prose against the diff. "boots a fresh copy of the same app (scratch: the same project; ask: a blank host with the same build installed the same way)" matches `freshBoot(ops, dir)` and the `withInstalledBuild` `fresh`. "it still counts in the `Run-operations` cell's `N started from restored rows`" matches the README and the untouched `scorecard.ts`. "Template mode keeps writing the rows back" matches `templateMode`, whose call passes no `fresh`. `Skills-docs:` is not owed: `Metadata-protocol: none`, and there is no narrowing arm.
- **README** (content checked against the diff): the two bullets match the code paths above.
- **Tests.**
  - New describe #34448, 3 cases on the real `asset_lifecycle.json` with a one-way-rule double (400 `VALIDATION_FAILED`, the card's own message). The positive case: six of six asked, `dispose_scrapped_asset` `restored: { freshCopy: ['demoasset_disposal_request/dr06'] }`, zero rule refusals, the booted app took only the seed's inserts and second-pass updates, and boots equal stops.
  - Two ⛔ cases: without a copy, the refusal is named, with no turn and no grade; a copy whose seed differs or that does not boot gives NOT MEASURED with its reason and is released. These are runner-level NOT-MEASURED outcomes, not HTTP refusals, so the ADR-0112 `code`/`status` assertion rule does not apply. The double's `VALIDATION_FAILED` + 400 is asserted verbatim in the reason string.
  - Ablation: `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, blob `f92b76b517ff` → `5cdc7e332873` with scratch given no copy, gives `-t 34448` 2 failed / 1 passed. The first case reproduces the card's failure. Restored to blob == HEAD.
- **Changed tests** (all named in the body). Each now asserts the new truth (`freshCopy` in place of `deleted`, `reinserted` or `setBack`; probes read across apps; the template host is the last booted app). None is loosened: the booted-app case gains an app-count assertion and an owners-equal-on-every-copy assertion.
  - The write-back path keeps its success coverage: the direct `restoreSeededRows` cases at test lines 3166–3185 (`setBack`, `reinserted`), and the replay cases at 1852 and 1898, still pin it.
  - Its refusal coverage moved to a template-style `runHalf` with no copy (`NoDeleteApp`, and no `deleteRow`), with the same reasons verbatim.
- **Gates (check-runs at `69b88800`, 53 runs).** 35 `success`, 18 path-filtered `skipped`, none red or pending. Required floor: Lint & Repo Gates `success`, TypeScript Type Check `success`. Test Core aggregate `success`, with planned shards 1–6/8 each `success` (the planner emitted six). Also `success`: Build Core, Check Changeset, Dogfood Regression Gate (aggregate) and the PR-body guards. Local `dispatch-gates --ran` on `69b88800`: 62/62, 0 NOT-MEASURED, a local subset only. The first-round exit 3s on `dc265d44` are explained and were rerun.
- **Nit (non-blocking, no rework).** In `moveToFreshCopy`, the bindings switch to the new copy before `await previous?.()`. If stopping the replaced copy throws, the `catch` releases the copy just switched to, the operation reads NOT MEASURED, and the half goes on against a stopped app (later operations then read NOT MEASURED, "could not be read"). This degrades to not-measured and never to a wrong grade. Releasing `previous` after the `try`, with its own `.catch`, would remove the edge. Optional here or in the template-mode follow-up.

**L2 owed: yes, at `TIER_DEFAULT` only.** The trigger is `Clause-②: yes (widening)`: `./runner` gains the type `FreshCopy`, `runHalf`'s optional `fresh` and `RowRestore.freshCopy`. No `packages/spec/src/**`, no governed rule text, no narrowing, so `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` is not owed. The seat routes it. No same-form PASS exists at this head yet, so at ACCEPT the dispatching seat adds `needs:contract-review` to the PR.

**Landing tier.** `node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 34490` reads: "0 of 4 path(s) hit the register … ✅ NOT governed — ordinary queue landing applies"; 411 changed lines ≤ 3000. Once both rework items are done and L2 PASS is recorded at the same head, the area lands it through the ordinary queue.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `69b88800e2ce07d7cf664de8af3c3430a6fd2d19`
Local-runs: none

Face: declaration only. The PR body and the changeset carry `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. The 4 changed paths hold no `packages/spec/src/**` file, no governed path (`check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 34490`: 0 of 4 hit the register) and no narrowing line, so `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` is not owed and there is no ④. Read on the diff `origin/main...69b88800` and the card thread's report 6931668123, at 2026-11-16T23:41Z.

### ① Derived judgments

- **What widens, through `./runner` only.** The new exported type `FreshCopy`; `runHalf` gains an optional LAST parameter `fresh?: FreshCopy`; `RowRestore` gains an optional field `freshCopy?: string[]`. The first `runHalf` parameter is renamed `app` → `firstApp`, which is positional and invisible to callers. No export is removed, no parameter becomes required, no existing field changes type. `./score`, `./score/full`, `./export` and `.` are untouched, as the changeset says.
- **Existing consumers of `RowRestore` hold.** The only reader outside `orchestrate.ts` is `scorecard.ts:386`, which counts `o.restored !== undefined`. A restore carrying only `freshCopy` is still counted in `N started from restored rows`, so the scorecard and the README sentence that says so stay true without a change to `scorecard.ts`.
- **A caller that passes no `fresh` gets the old behaviour exactly.** The `else` branch is the former `restoreSeededRows` call unchanged. The read loop moved into `seedDrift`, which returns the same `failed` text (`the rows of X could not be read to restore them: …`) that `restoreSeededRows` passes on. Template mode is that caller, with a comment at the call saying why.
- **With `fresh`, later turns really go to the copy.** `doorOf` and `keyOf` read the `let` bindings `app`, `adminKey` and `accounts` on each call, and `accounts` is spliced in place. So every later ask, confirmation and replay re-send goes to the copy. The first app stays owned by `withApp`. Each copy is released when it is replaced, when its seeding fails, and in the half's `finally`.
- **The documented contract matches the code.** The `FreshCopy` and `RowRestore.freshCopy` jsdoc, the `runHalf` docblock, the README bullets and the changeset prose each say that nothing is written to undo a move, that a copy whose seed differs (`seedDifference`: inserted count, refusals, permission-set assignment) makes the operation NOT MEASURED with the reason, and that template mode keeps the write-back. I checked each statement against the diff.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/scenarios`, the only package moved. Correct per AGENTS.md: "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`", and `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`. This matches the precedent #34338 (changeset `34294-scenario-restore-seeded-rows.md`, also a `./runner` widening shipped as `patch`). No BREAKING banner is owed: the change does not narrow anything.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev `open_questions` 6931668123: (1) Ask 2 isolation over a privileged restore door. Kept: it changes nothing the platform lets an HTTP caller do (`importControlOptOutRefusal` stands). (2) Clause-② `yes (widening)`. Agreed and recorded in the claim amendment 6931982958. (3) The template-mode follow-up is filed as #34497. (4) The README paragraph is on this PR, covered by the same amendment. (5) This record.
- `out_of_scope_findings`: Ask 4 (live `asset_lifecycle` 6/6) is NOT MEASURED and goes to the seat's gallery run. The PR says `Part of #34448`, and the card's close is arranged in 6932649454.
- L1 nit (6932638502): in `moveToFreshCopy` the bindings switch before `await previous?.()`, so a throwing stop of the replaced copy releases the new one too. This degrades only to NOT MEASURED, never to a wrong grade. Graded **nit**; accepted as is.
- SQL push-down: n/a. This is a test runner reading rows over HTTP with `listRows`. It adds no id materialisation or in-app join on a platform query path.
- Author: the PR was opened through the relay (`objectstack-fleet[bot]`), so no other login needs naming.
- Security-touching: no. Nothing in the diff changes what a caller is let do. The copies boot through the same `ops.boot` and `installUnmanaged` as the first app.
